items.quote: And Moses went up unto God, and the LORD called unto him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel;
items.claim: The text says Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain and told him to deliver a message to the house of Jacob, the children of Israel.
items.object: Moses; the house of Jacob, the children of Israel
items.place: the mountain (not named in this passage)
items.mechanism: divine speech given through Moses as messenger

items.quote: Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians,
items.claim: In the text, the LORD reminds Israel that they saw what he did to the Egyptians. The deeds themselves are not described in this passage.
items.mechanism: appeal to what Israel saw for themselves

items.quote: and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself.
items.claim: In the text, the LORD describes carrying Israel on eagles' wings and bringing them to himself. This is figurative language for deliverance.
items.action: bare ... on eagles' wings; brought ... unto myself
items.mechanism: metaphor (eagles' wings) for divine rescue and bringing Israel near
